text:
mike: quick heads-up: saw a stale-read in prod during demote+evict. short timeline: O1 demotes (epoch=77), accepts write W (inflight), slab reclaim evicts prefix, demote completes, O2 takes epoch=78 and serves read -> pre-W state.

tara: yikes. that suggests demote can finish while inflight writes only live in O1 RAM.

sasha: options: (1) block demote until inflight drains, (2) publish tiny fence metadata to control-plane + soft-pin, (3) read-side validation against old owner.

lee: (3) is brittle on crashes. prefer (2) as a balanced path: old owner publishes publish_fence(prefix,epoch,digest) and best-effort flushes to staging while setting a soft-pin so eviction is delayed. new owner waits T_handshake for fence, else RPC to old owner, else stall reads for safety.

mike: notes: fence must be idempotent and cheap. add durability modes: soft (meta only), durable (meta + staging), strict (meta + WAL) so tenants can pick tradeoffs.

tara: add telemetry: fence_published, fence_seen, reconcile_rpc, fence_latency, demote_blocked_count. also handoff_trace_id for correlating traces.

sasha: edge-case: if old owner crashes after fence publish but before flush, new owner may see fence but no data. need documented crash-fallback: stall then read-repair from backend.

lee: tests: chaos scenario - demote while slab reclaim + node crash + slow writes. validate no stale reads. add as non-blocking integration test.

mike: action items: mike: prototype fence+soft-pin + test (ETA: EOW). sasha: spec control-plane fence API (ETA: 3d). lee: telemetry + canary (ETA: 2d). tara: runbook update for crash fallback (ETA: 1d).

tara: :thumbsup: prioritise correctness for initial rollout; relax later with tenant flags.
